newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe Pipeline to shut segment of Ariz. line.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe Pipeline to shut segment of Ariz. line.

text.p: Santa Fe Pacific Pipeline Partners, L.P., plans to shut a 30-mile segment of pipeline entering Tucson, Arizona, this summer for planned repairs, a pipeline official said Wednesday.
Shipments on the eight-inch section will cease for three to four weeks during repairs, but will not cause shortages, said John Abboud, a senior vice president at the company.

Abboud said the company had not set specific dates for the shutdown but added they would occur in late summer or early fall. Shippers will be given sufficient warning so they can prepare for the lost line capacity.
The line carries 17,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of gasoline, jet fuel and diesel into Tucson from refiners in El Paso, Texas.
A 12-inch line linking the cities will continue to run, Abboud said, along with a 20-inch line coming from Los Angeles. The combined lines will bring in 245,000 bpd of refined products.
The repairs are part of five-year plan to replace the system's coating.
